verdicts.claim: 📐18's contact column is not on screen although the RPC already computes it: every row carries `owner` and `columns` declares no column for it.
verdicts.fix_hint: Not a fixer task — put cards-finance.md:372 item ✏️9.6 on Ishay's morning table with the new measurement (owner is populated on 100% of rows at every level, so the 📑ב#15 'column of all dashes' premise is now false); only on a 'draw it' ruling does the RPC add {key:'owner', label:'איש-קשר', format:'text', align:'start'} to v_columns (i1 migration, m09 level-0 list at ~line 1773 and the level-1/2 list at ~1842).
verdicts.reason: The absence reproduces on the current tree: the i1 migration's m09 v_columns (both branches) lists 7 / 4 / 5 keys with no owner, while the same function selects customer_contacts.contact_name as 'owner' into every row (verified in the file this turn), and the live payloads show owner filled on every row. processes-approved.md:870 does require the column. But the owner is not the RPC: micro-guide line 171 defines the contract as rows carrying 'owner' BESIDE drill_key, i.e. outside columns, and cards-finance.md:372 records ✏️9.6 as 🔵 פתוח — a DELIBERATE declared abstention ('לא ציירתי עמודה שכולה —', 📑ב#15) that asks Ishay to approve it or order the names measured first. Routing it to a fixer would silently overrule a pending product decision. What is new and worth surfacing is that the abstention's sole premise is now measured false.

verdicts.claim: The table's sort key (₪) is contradicted by two onboarding sentences and by the 'אז מה' line on the same screen — the user is told to start at the top row because its PERCENT is the largest, and it is not.
verdicts.fix_hint: One D-29-shaped ruling: the sort stays ₪ (processes-approved.md:864 📑ב#5 is tier-2 and names the sort; the mockup is tier-4) and the two hint sentences are corrected in src/lib/onboardingCopy.m11.finance.js:56 ('…כי סכום-הסטייה שלו הוא הגדול ביותר') and :64 (drop 'והטבלה לפי אחוז-הסטייה'), with cards-finance.md §⑩ א/ג + item ⑧8.7 closed in Phase 4 — the RPC and the tab need no change.
verdicts.reason: Reproduces at the source on the current tree. The i1 migration's m08 rows are ordered '(planned_hours<4 or planned_labor<1000), budget_deviation desc' and meta.sort is null, so the shipped table ranks by ₪ — which is what processes-approved.md:864 locks ('מיון ברירת-מחדל לפי ₪-חריגה ולא לפי %'), and financePayload.jsx's own comment says so. The two sentences that ship beside it still assert the opposite: onboardingCopy.m11.finance.js:56 'התחילי מהפרויקט שבראש הטבלה, כי אחוז-הסטייה שלו הוא הגדול ביותר' and :64 'הגרף ממוין לפי גודל-הסטייה ב-₪ והטבלה לפי אחוז-הסטייה', both copied verbatim from cards-finance.md §⑩ א/ג per C3; the live payload's top row is 21.1% while the so_what line names 1427 at 27.2% (4th row). No ruling covers it — D-29 ruled only reports.aging.whyAndFirst, and grep of §9 finds nothing on m08's sort (D-27 is m07's card 8.7.5). The card's own ⑧8.7 is still 🔵 פתוח and predicted exactly this ('המסך החי ימיין לפי ₪ — ואז שמונה השורות יהיו אחרות'), which is why this is one ruling and not a patch.

verdicts.claim: The chart '15 הסטיות הגדולות ב-₪' renders 15 exclusively NEGATIVE bars — the fifteen biggest SAVINGS — on a page asking 'אילו פרויקטים דלפו מהתקציב?', and not one of the 15 appears in the table.
verdicts.fix_hint: No build change — if Ishay wants the chart to answer the page's question it is a new ruling (order by budget_deviation desc instead of abs, and retitle '15 החריגות הגדולות'); until then the measurement (all 15 negative, intersection 0 with the table's 30 rows) belongs on the morning table, not in a fixer queue.
verdicts.reason: Refuted as a defect: the build implements the approved drawing exactly. cards-finance.md מ8 §③ specifies 'גרף — סטיית-תקציב ב-₪, top-15 חתום … ממוין לפי גודל מוחלט; ציר −1,000…+1,000, קו-אפס', and the i1 migration does precisely that ('order by abs(budget_deviation) desc limit 15', with the comment quoting 📊 · 📑ב#5). The disjointness from the table is not an unnoticed consequence either — the card's own ⑧8.4 states 'פרויקט 12 אינו ב-15 הגדולים ב-₪ — וזה בדיוק הממצא'. The measurement itself is true (m08_baseline chart data −2,688/−2,408/−2,346…, 15 items, project_id intersection with the 30 rows = 0), and the shared layer already used it to switch cross-filter off; as a product question it is Ishay's, not the RPC's.

verdicts.claim: The מדרג column renders every bucket range MIRRORED — '1–30' as '30–1', '61–90' as '90–61', '90+' as '+90' — while the chart's x-axis on the same page shows them correctly.

The chart axis is unaffected only because ChartCard wraps the figure in dir='ltr'. No ruling covers it — D-32 introduced these labels in this very round and D-26 is the house precedent mandating isolation for exactly this shape; check:bidi is green by its own admission (scripts/check-bidi-glyphs.mjs:13-16). Not the routed מ9 item (chart.note).

verdicts.claim: The same mirroring hits RPC-authored strings the tab cannot reach: tile 'מדרג 90+' renders 'מדרג +90', the crumb and level-1 tile mirror the same way, and the export file name inherits it.

verdicts.claim: The empty-after-filter envelope (📐10 state 2, 'אין חשבוניות פתוחות בתקופה שנבחרה · [נקה מסננים]') can never appear on this tab: the shell shows it only when tiles AND charts AND rows are all empty, and all four finance RPCs always return 4–5 tiles.

Measured live: customer 231 returns 5 tiles with 0 rows and 0 chart data, and the browser showed the table card with an empty tbody, no sentence and no clear-filters button; the only signal is the 11px EXPORT_NO_ROWS caption. The rulings go the other way: no D-item touches the envelope gate, and cards-finance.md:160 declares the state verbatim with rows 112/225/405/492/579 specifying 'טבלה ריקה ⇒ ריק-אחרי-סינון'. Kept at major, not raised: the tiles do show true zeroes, so this is a missing state plus a missing escape hatch, not a false number — but one shell fix restores it across all sixteen surfaces.

verdicts.claim: The test called 'רמה 2 · ארבעת הרמזים של מבט-על מצוירים בעוגנים שלהם' never measures an anchor — it only asserts each hint is in the document.
verdicts.fix_hint: FinanceTab.test.jsx:694-702 — either assert document order against the surface's own regions (compareDocumentPosition of hint-reports.overview.tileBasis vs the chart card, hint-…oldestSort vs report-table-card) or rename the test to what it measures ('ארבעת הרמזים מוצגים'); a name that promises anchors while asserting presence is the part that misleads.
verdicts.reason: Reproduces verbatim at HEAD: the whole body is a loop of expect(screen.getByTestId('hint-'+id)).toBeInTheDocument(), with no order or parent assertion, so a build that stacked all four hints at the bottom would pass. Downgraded from major to minor because what it fails to catch is itself a minor placement issue (index 10) and the assertion it does make is correct — the defect is a test NAME that certifies more than the test measures, not a false green on user-visible data.

verdicts.claim: The test written FOR the bucket-label defect cannot see the defect that shipped: it asserts DOM containment of '90+' and '61–90', and jsdom has no bidi layout, so the mirrored rendering passes it.
verdicts.fix_hint: Leave the jsdom test as is and add the missing channel: a Playwright case in e2e/reports.spec.js that opens מ9 and asserts, with a per-character Range.getBoundingClientRect probe, that the מדרג cell's digits render in logical order — the one measurement scripts/check-bidi-glyphs.mjs:13-16 says it cannot make.
verdicts.reason: The mechanical claim is true (the shipped page satisfies all three assertions while rendering '30–1'/'+90'), but the framing is half wrong and that is why it is not major: the test's own name is 'עמודת מדרג מציגה תוויות-מסך ולא מפתחות-מסד' — it was written for the D-32 raw-key defect and it does catch that; it never claimed to measure rendering order, and no jsdom test can. The real content is a coverage gap in a channel the repo already documents as missing, and the defect it would catch is separately routed as index 6.
